news.title: Quantum trick lets you share your location super securely
paras: Facebook Threads X / Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Reddit Email Print NIST’s campus in Boulder, Colorado NIST Financial institutions and critical infrastructure could be made far more secure in the near-future using quantum particles.

For years, researchers have predicted that quantum particles could enable someone to share their location, and to verify someone else’s, in a way that is exceedingly difficult to hack. This would allow one branch of a bank to confirm that a request for funds or client information is coming from another branch and not from a hacker.

news.title: 'A shotgun marriage': Why are NASA's SkyFall Mars helicopters riding on a nuclear rocket?
paras: "The connection to Space Reactor-1 seems to me to be a bit of a shotgun marriage, a tech-demo piggybacking on another mission as an opening bid for a 'nuclear NASA.'" NASA's Skyfall mission will see those mini-choppers dropped off at Mars by the space agency's Space Reactor-1 Freedom (SR-1) rocket, the first fission nuclear-powered interplanetary spacecraft slated for launch in late 2028.

But some experts are questioning why NASA is combining two such high-profile missions into one. "It is clear that SkyFall was approved for programmatic or political reasons," said Scott Hubbard, former director of NASA's Ames Research Center and the first Mars Program Director (aka the " Mars Czar ") at NASA Headquarters, told Space.com.

news.title: Supernova explodes before astronomers' eyes | Space photo of the day for Nov. 18, 2026
paras: A new supernova has been spotted exploding in the spiral galaxy NGC 1433, about 50 million light-years from Earth. Researchers have discovered a new supernova called SN 2026ahvu.

A Type Ia supernova, this event took place in a system with two stars orbiting one another (also known as a binary system), in which typically one star is an exploding white dwarf . During most type Ia supernovae, the white dwarf pulls material away from the other star until enough accumulates on its surface to create an explosion. Finding galaxies where stellar explosions are taking place isn't a rarity.

news.title: Why do female bonobos have so much power?
paras: In many animal groups, power often belongs to the biggest and strongest individuals. Male bonobos are usually larger than females. But females often have higher social status.

We studied six wild bonobo communities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. We looked at conflicts between males and females. We also looked at female coalitions, when two or more females worked together to attack another individual. We found the strongest support for the idea that females had more power when they formed coalitions.

news.title: Chihuahuas Seem to Carry a Tiny Bit of Coyote DNA—but That's Probably Not Why They Have Fearless Personalities
paras: Add as preferred source Chihuahuas are the smallest recognized dog breed. Pexels Thousands of years ago, the ancestors of Chihuahuas mated with wild coyotes.

Today, traces of that ancient interbreeding live on in the DNA of the popular pint-size dogs—but they likely aren’t responsible for the creatures’ fearless personalities. A study published in July in the journal Nature Communications has found a sliver of coyote DNA buried in the Chihuahua genome, their complete set of genetic material. Researchers don’t know exactly when coyote DNA entered the tiny pooch’s gene pool, but their findings suggest the genetic link arose long ago, before Europeans arrived in the Americas.
